name: CRS-35 · Cargo Dragon to the ISS
launchSite: Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, SLC-40
summary: SpaceX’s 35th commercial resupply mission launched from SLC-40 on 13 October 2026 and docked to Harmony’s space-facing port at 10:27 a.m. EDT on 15 October — about 30 minutes early — with more than 6,300 lb of cargo and the station’s final pair of roll-out solar arrays.

articles.title: Cargo Dragon docks with the station’s last new solar arrays
Dragon flies the last of the station’s 8 new solar wings

fidelityNote: Event times are verified. Dragon’s approach path is an illustrative reconstruction. The ISS orbit shown during replay is a calculated segment from current CelesTrak elements, not October 2026 ephemeris. Historical orbital replay needs historical elements; those are not in this snapshot.

events.label: Liftoff
events.source: Supercharged Daily CRS-35 launch dispatch, citing SpaceX: 6:33 a.m. ET (3:33 a.m. PT) on 13 Oct 2026. https://superchargeddaily.com/dispatch/crs35-final-solar-arrays.html

events.label: Orbit raising (about 52 hours)
events.source: SpaceX CRS-35 mission page, via Supercharged Daily: trip put at about 52 hours.
events.note: No public burn-by-burn ephemeris is included. The globe shows the ISS calculated orbit, not Dragon’s phasing burns.

events.label: Dragon 10 metres from the station
events.source: SpaceX on X, 10:24 a.m. ET, 15 Oct 2026, cited in https://superchargeddaily.com/dispatch/crs35-dragon-docks.html

events.label: Docking confirmed · Harmony zenith
